motion.name: camera
motion.value: smoothstep over the middle 80% of each stop, then exponential damping (k = 1 - exp(-dt * 3.4))
motion.purpose: Camera walk between the six stops; jumps under reduced motion.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Panels at rest, camera jumps, timeline fully filled.

scene.renderer: three@0.160, ACES Filmic tone mapping, exposure .98, sRGB output, RoomEnvironment env map at .55, background #eeebe6

lighting.name: ceiling
lighting.value: PointLight #fff6ea, 9 (6 on the light path) + second PointLight 5 (desktop only)

scene.shadows: VSMShadowMap, 2048 map, radius 10, 16 blur samples; autoUpdate off, recomputed only when a chair swivels; render loop stops after about 30 still frames

components.css: :host{--papier:#f6f5f2;--teinte:#ebebe9;--lac:#1f1c1a;--nuit:#1a1614;--cuivre:#b4441d;--cuivre-fonce:#973818;--ecume:#f2b49a;--gris:#5e5853;--sur-nuit:#bdb4ab;--filet:rgba(31,28,26,.16);--filet-clair:rgba(246,245,242,.18);--ease:cubic-bezier(.22,.8,.24,1)}.ds-carte{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:16px;padding:18px 20px;border-radius:18px;background:#2a2421;color:var(--papier);text-decoration:none;font-family:Archivo,'Helvetica Neue',Arial,sans-serif;transition:background-color .2s,transform .16s var(--ease)}.ds-carte:hover{background:#352d29}.ds-carte:active{transform:scale(.98)}.ds-carte:focus-visible{outline:3px solid var(--cuivre);outline-offset:3px}.ds-onde{position:relative;flex:none;width:54px;height:54px;border-radius:50%;background:var(--cuivre);color:#fff;display:grid;place-items:center}.ds-onde::after{content:'';position:absolute;inset:0;border-radius:50%;box-shadow:0 0 0 0 rgba(180,68,29,.6);animation:ds-onde 2.4s var(--ease) infinite}@keyframes ds-onde{70%,100%{box-shadow:0 0 0 16px rgba(180,68,29,0)}}@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.ds-onde::after{animation:none}}.ds-onde .ds-ico{width:24px;height:24px}.ds-ico{width:1.15em;height:1.15em;flex:none;fill:none;stroke:currentColor;stroke-width:1.9;stroke-linejoin:round;stroke-linecap:round}.ds-txt{display:grid;gap:2px}.ds-lib{font-size:14px;font-weight:600;color:var(--sur-nuit)}.ds-tel{font-weight:900;font-stretch:112%;font-size:34px;line-height:1.05;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;white-space:nowrap}.ds-statut{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;font-size:14px;color:var(--sur-nuit)}.ds-statut i{width:9px;height:9px;border-radius:50%;background:var(--sur-nuit)}.ds-ouvert i{background:#5fd38a;box-shadow:0 0 0 3px rgba(95,211,138,.2)}

narrative.overview:
The site is the salon itself, by day. A fixed WebGL scene rebuilds the real room (white walls, a grey painted-brick back wall with the sign, brown 30 cm floor tiles, two black quilted barber chairs marked Elle and Lui, bonnet dryers along the windows, moulded shell waiting chairs, big windows with sky and the boulevard behind). Scrolling walks the camera from the sidewalk through six stops: entrance, chairs, salon, waiting corner, counter, contact. At each stop one solid paper panel holds the words. The panel sits on the left or the right, and the camera shifts the room away from it.

Density is low: one panel per stop, about 500px wide, with long scroll between stops so the room carries the page. Everything in a panel is plain, matte paper with charcoal ink and one copper accent. The only dark surface is the contact panel (and the footer and mobile menu that extend it). The room stays in daylight even at the contact stop. One variable family, Archivo, carries every voice on its width axis. Section titles follow the house standard: three fitted uppercase lines, the second outlined and the third in copper, under a small copper kicker. The imagery is the rendered room. There are no salon photos, no video and no old logo.
keyCharacteristics: A daylight 3D room fills the viewport; solid paper panels float over it, never glass.
One typeface, many widths: Archivo variable (wdth 62 to 125, wght 100 to 900), self-hosted.
Fitted three-line titles: solid, outlined, copper.
Copper is the action colour: pill buttons, kicker, rules that fill, the call icon.
Night lives only in the contact panel, the footer and the mobile menu.
The phone number is tabular, never wraps, and is reachable from every viewport.

rules.name: The Copper Acts Rule
rules.body: Copper marks what you can do or where you are: buttons, the kicker, underlines, the filling timeline, the active dot. It is never a panel or section fill.

rules.name: The Foam On Night Rule
rules.body: On night surfaces every copper role switches to Copper Foam. Copper text on night measures 3.24:1 and is not used. The copper call icon on the night card is a filled graphic with a white glyph, not text.

rules.name: The Night Is Contained Rule
rules.body: The world is light. Night is a panel, never the room: the contact stop keeps the 3D salon in daylight, and only the contact panel, footer and mobile menu turn dark.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Every voice is Archivo. Contrast comes from width (wdth 62 to 125) and weight, never from a second typeface or a system display face.

rules.name: The Fitted Title Rule
rules.body: Every panel's title is exactly three lines, each fitted to the column width: solid, outlined, accent. Set it with the `.ajuste` fitting script; never with a fixed width or by hand.

rules.name: The Kicker Rule
rules.body: Per the user's house standard (site-3d-interactif-pme), each fitted title sits under one kicker: a short copper dash and a place or role in spaced capitals ("749, boulevard Cadieux", "Les deux chaises"). One kicker per panel, and it names the stop, not a marketing tag.

rules.name: The Tabular Phone Rule
rules.body: Phone numbers and durations are tabular and never wrap.

rules.name: The Solid Panel Rule
rules.body: Content panels are opaque paper (or opaque night). Never put glass or blur behind words over the scene. Translucency belongs to the header and the mobile call bar alone.

rules.name: The Daylight Room Rule
rules.body: The 3D room is always lit by day, at every stop, including contact. Mood never comes from darkening the scene.

dos: **Do** put every block of words on one solid paper panel (Panel Paper, 22px corners, panel shadow) over the 3D room, aligned left or right, one panel per stop.
**Do** head each panel with one copper kicker and a three-line fitted title: solid, outlined, copper (Foam on night).
**Do** make every action a pill: Copper for the call and booking, Ink for moving on, Clear on dark.
**Do** switch every copper role to Copper Foam on night surfaces.
**Do** keep the phone number tabular, unwrapped, and one tap away on every viewport (header, hero, call card, mobile bar).
**Do** change voice through Archivo's width axis: condensed and fitted for titles, extended for the brand and the number.
**Do** keep the room in daylight at every stop and keep the lighter mobile 3D path (no shadow maps, pixel ratio 1.5, metal-plane mirrors, one ceiling light).
**Do** use the single easing `cubic-bezier(.22, .8, .24, 1)` and honour reduced motion everywhere.
donts: **Don't** put glass, blur or translucency behind panel text; translucency is for the header and mobile bar only.
**Don't** darken the room or make night the world; night is the contact panel, the footer and the mobile menu.
**Don't** add a second typeface or fall back to a system display face.
**Don't** set Copper text on night (3.24:1); use Copper Foam.
**Don't** fill a panel or section with copper.
**Don't** quilt the dryer chairs; capitonné belongs to the two barber chairs.
**Don't** add hard offset shadows; elevation is the soft Ink-tinted ambient shadow.
**Don't** introduce salon photos, video or the old logo, and never present renders as real work; the imagery is the rendered room.
**Don't** invent reviews, ratings, years or services; the review carousel stays hidden until exact review texts are supplied, and every figure must be one the salon has confirmed.
